ask: Which SuiteSuccess edition is being quoted, and exactly which modules does it include?
why: The edition sets the baseline. Everything below is either in it or an add-on.

ask: Is OneWorld included, and what does adding a subsidiary later cost?
why: Retrofitting OneWorld is a migration. Price the option now even if not exercised.

ask: Advanced Revenue Management: in scope or not?
why: Expensive, one-way. Prepaid plans and gift cards usually force it; charge-on-ship may not.

ask: Which manufacturing tier: Work Orders only, WIP & Routings, or Advanced Manufacturing?
why: Determines costing depth and shop-floor capability.
Sets when costing posts and whether freight and duty reach item cost.

ask: SuiteTax or legacy Advanced Taxes, and is a tax partner (Avalara etc.) needed?
why: One-way, and it touches every sales transaction.

ask: Quality Management SuiteApp: needed, and what does it cost?
why: Only if formal inspection records are required. Inventory Status alone may be enough.

ask: Demand Planning: can it come off the quote if the forecast stays external?
why: Likely a straight removal if the external forecast tool is staying.

ask: NetSuite Planning & Budgeting vs native budgets?
why: Native budgets are included and cover most budget-vs-actual needs.

ask: WMS or a third-party scanning solution: needed for receiving, picking, and lot capture?
why: Drives whether floor staff need licenses and whether lot capture is realistic.

ask: Catch weight: what is the supported approach and what does it cost?
why: No native support. If yes, this must be priced before signature.

ask: Minimum remaining shelf life enforcement: native, SuiteApp, or custom?
why: Not native. If customers mandate it, it is unscoped work.

ask: How many full user licenses vs Employee / Customer / Vendor Center, and what does each cost?
why: Licensing is per unique login by role. This is a recurring cost that compounds.

ask: Which sandbox tier is included, and what does a Premium sandbox cost?
why: Roughly 10% of subscription for standard, ~20% for premium. Needed for item-load dry runs.

ask: Integration approach: native connectors, an iPaaS, or custom - and who builds each?
why: Usually the largest variable line in the whole implementation cost.

ask: How much history is being migrated, and is that priced?
why: Migration scope is a cost driver that is easy to leave vague until it is expensive.

ask: What is the annual uplift cap at renewal?
why: Not a discovery question, but the one most often left unasked before signature.
